rule.title: ecrecover used on state-changing path without nonce increment to prevent signature replay

intent.attack_thesis: A function verifies a signature via ecrecover (precompile address 0x1) on a state-changing path but does not increment a nonce associated with the recovered signer. The same signature can be replayed indefinitely to repeat the authorized action.

reporting.title_template: Signature replay attack: ecrecover without nonce protection on state-changing path
reporting.summary: Matches functions that call ecrecover (precompile 0x1) on a path with state-changing effects but do not increment a per-signer nonce in storage.
reporting.user_summary: This function verifies a cryptographic signature but does not track used signatures with a nonce. An attacker who captures a valid signature can replay it repeatedly to repeat the authorized action — withdrawing funds, minting tokens, or executing privileged operations — as many times as they like.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies functions where ecrecover (CALL to precompile 0x1) appears on a state-changing path (asset_transfer, mint, accounting_mutation) without a corresponding SLOAD-increment-SSTORE pattern for a nonce slot associated with the recovered address. This allows indefinite replay of any valid signature.
reporting.exploit_narrative: A user signs a meta-transaction or off-chain authorization. The attacker intercepts the signature and replays the same transaction repeatedly. Each replay executes the authorized action again — draining funds, minting extra tokens, or applying double credits — until the attacker is satisfied.
exploit_preconditions: contract validates a signature via ecrecover
no nonce, deadline, or used-signature tracking prevents replay
signed action has material economic effect
remediation_hints: add a per-address nonce mapping (nonces[signer]++) and include the nonce in the signed message
use OZ Nonces (EIP-4337 compatible) or equivalent well-audited nonce management
include a deadline in the signed message and reject expired signatures
adopt EIP-712 typed signing with a domain separator to bind signatures to the specific contract and chain

preconditions: valid signature captured (e.g., from mempool or off-chain API)
contract does not track used signatures

steps.action: call function with replayed signature (same r, s, v, message hash as original)
steps.expected_state: signature validates successfully; authorized effect executed again

steps.action: repeat call with same signature until objective achieved
steps.expected_state: repeated execution extracts value proportional to signature reuse count

witness_goal.success_condition: same signature executes authorized action N>1 times without the signer's consent
